witnesses.hypothesis: An arrow is one 8-connected object, so a fletching set back by a gap belongs to no head. The head then has no fletching and reads no heading, the loose fletching has no head, and neither flies: the output is all background. The peer model that gathers around each head the marks nearest it keeps this fletching with its head and flies the arrow right, its point to the last column, giving row 2 `8 8 8 1 8 8 8 8 2 8`, row 3 `8 8 8 8 1 1 8 3 4 9`, and row 4 `8 8 8 1 8 8 8 8 6 8`.

The heading comes from where the fletching lies, not from the cell it touches. This fletching meets the bottom arm at that arm's two corners, and it lies wholly below the center, so the arrow reads as pointing up and flies up. The peer model that reads the heading off the cell one step beyond an arm finds no fletching cell there and leaves the grid all background.
violates: the fletching's nearest cell lies one step beyond the back arm

witnesses.hypothesis: The head is the center with its four cardinal neighbors, and the fletching is whatever else the object holds, so color tells neither part. This arrow's back arm carries the fletching's color 1; this model still reads that cell as an arm, turns it to the front, and flies the arrow up 2. The peer model that reads the fletching as the cells of a stored fletching color counts that arm into the fletching, leaves the head with three arms, and has no partner for the half turn.
violates: the head's arms and the fletching carry no color in common

witnesses.hypothesis: A flight ends at the grid edge and at nothing else. These two arrows share a lane and point at each other, so they pass through one another and swap sides. The peer model that halts a flight on contact with another arrow stops both near the middle of the lane instead.
violates: an arrow's flight lane holds no other arrow
